$comment: P1-28 traceability record (P1-28-DOC-001), checked by
scripts/ci/check-p1-28-traceability.mjs (validate:p1-28-traceability).
WHAT THIS IS. The binding between the canonical 35-task register and the
tree: which operation each task consumes, which permission that operation
publishes, and which EXECUTABLE CASES prove the canonical test id the plan
allocated to it.
WHY IT IS DATA AND NOT PROSE. P1-27 declared twenty-nine TC ids across three
documents and a repository-wide search returned nothing for any of them: the
plan said each 'will expand into the required path matrix', a future tense
nobody ever discharged. Twenty-nine empty test files would have made that
search succeed and proved nothing. So a citation here names a FILE and quotes
CASE TITLES, the titles are matched against comment-stripped source, and a
renamed case breaks the record instead of quietly hollowing it out.
EVERY PATH IN A `surface` IS REPOSITORY-RELATIVE AND IS RESOLVED. That
sentence used to be a promise this file made and the gate did not keep: the
checker tested `surface` for NON-EMPTINESS only, so pointing a task at
`NoSuchFile.tsx:4242` still reported zero disagreements — and seven surfaces
were in fact naming files that had never existed or had been renamed
(`IdentityStep`, `FuelStep`, `ComplaintStep`, `DamageStep`, `steps.ts`,
`ReceptionAcknowledgementScreen`, and a conversion section attributed to
`SummaryStep.tsx`). The gate now extracts every path-shaped token from each
surface, resolves it against the repository root — ONE root, which is why
these read `apps/web/src/...` rather than `features/...` — and, where a
`:LINE` is cited, requires that the file has that line and that the line is
not blank. Every task must resolve at least one path; a surface that names
no file is a surface nobody can check.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. No count that the tree can answer. The apt/rec surface
figures, the task-category sizes, the reachability classification counts and
the matrix totals are all derived by the gate and substituted into the
documents that carry a `derived:` marker. A number written here by hand would
be a number that goes stale, which is the exact defect this record exists to
close. The three totals below are the record's own shape, not the tree's, and
the gate recomputes them from these rows.
THE BROWSER COLUMN IS DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. `provenBy` is the mocked tier:
component and contract suites that mock the transport, which is a test
fixture and NOT production-integration evidence (canonical-plan.md section
10). `observedInBrowserBy` may only cite apps/web/tests/e2e/**, where a real
session reaches the real Next.js server, the real API and the real database.
The gate refuses any other path in that field.

permissions.apt.appointment.manage: Books and reschedules. FE-002 and FE-003 consult it; confirming is a side effect of reschedule, so this one code carries both.
permissions.apt.appointment.lifecycle.manage: Ends an appointment against the customer — cancel and no-show. A DIFFERENT code from booking, deliberately, and FE-004/FE-005 gate on it alone.
permissions.apt.appointment.read: The appointment list, detail and the three operator-facing appointment catalogue reads. Seeded by R2 (PR #220); before it no apt.*.read code existed anywhere.
permissions.apt.catalogue.manage: The nine appointment catalogue management writes and the three management reads PR #227 registered. Granted to NO role by any seed: P1-28-OD-001.
permissions.rec.reception.manage: Opens a visit. FE-007's create form is withdrawn without it, and the read permission still keeps the resume path.
permissions.rec.reception.read: The six per-visit reads, the queue and the four operator-facing reception catalogue reads. Seeded by R1 (PR #220); it is what lifted the single-session limitation.
permissions.rec.reception.party.manage: Records a party role on the visit (FE-009).
permissions.rec.reception.authorization.verify: Records an authorization decision (FE-009). High risk, approval audit class.
permissions.rec.reception.evidence.manage: All eight condition-evidence kinds (FE-010 … FE-016). For complaint and contents the DATABASE additionally requires iam.sensitive.view — WF-27, recorded in composed-permissions.json.
permissions.rec.reception.signature.manage: The signature record and the refusal record (FE-018, FE-019) — one code, two different operations.
permissions.rec.reception.approve: Approves the visit (FE-020). Above being able to record evidence.
permissions.rec.reception.close: The two terminal exits R5 added, close-without-work and refuse (FE-020). A third authority again.
permissions.rec.reception.convert: Converts a visit into a work order (FE-022). NOT a wo.* code — WF-12.
permissions.rec.catalogue.manage: The twelve reception catalogue management writes and the four management reads PR #227 registered. Granted to NO role by any seed: P1-28-OD-001.
